title: WWT Partners Weekly Briefing
description: Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, F5, Intel, NVIDIA, Microsoft, Palo Alto Networks, AWS, Google Cloud and VMware.
readFirst: Covers Nov. 9–16. New: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 14 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent questioned whether Nvidia knowingly sold AI GPUs to pass-through shell companies and said people at the company should be held accountable. No Red Hat press release or Army or Department of War Red Hat deal dated Nov. 13–16 was found. No new Army or Department of War enterprise agreement was found. No new Cisco, Dell, HPE, NetApp, Microsoft, AWS, or Google Cloud newsroom item dated Nov. 13–16 was opened. Unit 42's Cairn report is on the cyber page. F5, Intel, and VMware were quiet.

items.headline: Nvidia says Jensen Huang resigned and Colette Kress is interim chief executive
items.summary: NVIDIA said Nov. 12 that Jensen Huang resigned as president, chief executive, and a member of the board, effective immediately. The company said Colette Kress, executive vice president and chief financial officer since September 2013, will serve as interim chief executive while remaining chief financial officer, and that the board, now chaired for the first time by Harvey C. Jones, will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent successor. Jones said the board expects operations, customer commitments, and the product roadmap to continue without interruption. NVIDIA said it will still report fiscal 2027 third-quarter results on Nov. 17.

items.headline: Bessent questions whether Nvidia sold AI GPUs to pass-through shell companies
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 14 that Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, in a CNBC interview, said there is a lot of leakage in export controls and that the question is whether Nvidia knew its clients and made a robust effort not to sell to pass-through shell companies. Bessent said anyone at the company should be held accountable for that. Tom's Hardware said Bessent does not believe the United States needs stricter export restrictions or additional agency powers, and that existing rules should be enforced. Tom's Hardware also said Bessent stressed that it was unclear whether Jensen Huang knew about the practices.

items.headline: Tom's Hardware: SemiAnalysis estimates 1.5 gigawatts of restricted Nvidia hardware reached China
items.summary: Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 13 that SemiAnalysis estimates more than 1.5 gigawatts of Nvidia hardware subject to U.S. export restrictions reached China in recent years, not counting chips Nvidia designed to comply with those rules, such as the H20 and H800. Tom's Hardware said SemiAnalysis claims the Commerce Department has reached a similar conclusion about the scale, and that the firm did not disclose how many accelerators were involved or how they split across product generations. Tom's Hardware said the newsletter speculates that this scale may explain the timing of Jensen Huang's departure, and that the report provides no direct evidence that intelligence agencies influenced Nvidia's board or that Huang took part in unauthorized exports.

items.headline: Rosen Law Firm says it filed a securities class action over Huang and Megaspeed
items.summary: GlobeNewswire carried a Nov. 9 Rosen Law Firm release saying the firm filed a securities class action for purchasers of Nvidia securities from Oct. 9, 2025, through Nov. 8, 2026, and that a lead-plaintiff motion is due Jan. 8, 2027. The release says the complaint alleges Jensen Huang had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy who has a role at Megaspeed, which the suit says is suspected of helping China evade export controls, and that Nvidia's statements about its relationship with Megaspeed were materially false. It says the suit claims those facts raised national-security concerns and a risk to the company's reputation, and that investors suffered damages when the details entered the market. Tom's Hardware reported Nov. 10 that Rosen's filing was the first class action in the matter.

items.headline: OpenAI lists ChatGPT Enterprise in AWS Marketplace against existing AWS commitments
items.summary: OpenAI said Nov. 9 that ChatGPT Enterprise is available through AWS Marketplace, so organizations can buy and manage it through an existing AWS purchasing and billing relationship and apply eligible spend toward AWS commitments. OpenAI said AWS customers get the same models, features, and functionality available directly from OpenAI, including ChatGPT, ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots, with new features released at the same time. OpenAI said the listing complements OpenAI models in Amazon Bedrock, and that eligible customers can also access ChatGPT for Healthcare and ChatGPT for Financial Services through the marketplace. Chris Grusz, OpenAI's managing director for cloud partnerships, said joint customers can bring ChatGPT to their teams through AWS.

items.headline: Red Hat makes OpenShift 5 generally available, with post-quantum control-plane cryptography
items.summary: Red Hat said Nov. 9 at KubeCon in Salt Lake City that Red Hat OpenShift 5 is generally available to customers with existing subscriptions, as an in-place update from OpenShift 4. Red Hat said the release runs AI workloads, virtual machines, and containers side by side, and that OpenShift Lightspeed moves from a conversational assistant to an agent that can troubleshoot and assess update risk. Red Hat said the release adds Model Context Protocol server support and post-quantum cryptography for control-plane communications, plus hardened multi-tenancy for sovereign and disconnected deployments. Chief product officer Ashesh Badani said the release includes a five-year predictable lifecycle.

items.headline: Red Hat says Enterprise Linux 10.3 and 9.9 will add sealed images and disconnected AI help
items.summary: Red Hat said Nov. 9 at KubeCon in Salt Lake City that Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.3 and 9.9 are planned to be generally available in the coming weeks. Red Hat said 10.3 introduces sealed images for image mode so customers can sign and verify the operating system with their own keys and block unauthorized components at runtime. Red Hat said a Model Context Protocol server can investigate live systems with governed access, and that a developer-preview command-line assistant can run on customer-hosted inference for disconnected or air-gapped sites. Red Hat said 10.3 also adds post-quantum cryptography in the Go toolchain.
